goal_title: Book: Randomness: What Can Chance Change? — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in randomness became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note
the chapters read through without a stumble in the headset
every code excerpt and number in the chapters matches the source

reading.arc: The sequence takes one verb, draw, and gives it fourteen jobs. A seed becomes a picture only through a procedure (Definition); a gauge condenses a sample and forgets its order (Entropy); a rule fixes the eligible set before chance picks, and a second piece of code turns a disappearance into a fall (Remove); two marks become contours, a floor, slabs at shoulder width and an ant's map (10 PRINT); a thrown die is read from its orientation and kept as frequencies (Cubes); turning accumulates without a trail (Rotate); a trail is kept but never consulted (Walk); a histogram's shape is a matter of law, clipping and bins (Gaussian); a wardrobe samples within a recipe that chance cannot extend (Mushrooms); neighbours share or do not (Geometry); chance gets four different jobs in a gallery (Examples); a mark enters the next decision (Pheromone); layers add up to something that looks like land (Space); and the closing crossing asks which decisions are already made and which a body must still find out (Game). The through-line is a refusal to let the word random cover three decisions at once: what may vary, how it is drawn, and what is kept. The reader is asked again and again to predict before pressing, and to compare records that forget different things.
holds: The refrain of three decisions folded into one word: "Filter, draw, delete… only the middle one is" (Remove) returns as palette / line rule / canvas (Examples), wardrobe vs construction (Mushrooms), sampling / clipping / binning (Gaussian), and stands / leaves / gone / returns (Game).

The seed as a name that is not the whole recipe: seed + generator + calls + use (Definition) → "Changing modes retains the seed but spends its draws differently" (Walk) → "a seed is not a promise that every branch of a program spends its draws in the same way" (Mushrooms), carried by a REPLAY / NEW SEED console in almost every hall (board, floor, terrarium, sampler, silhouettes, couture, crossing, doors, podium).

Records that forget different things: the gauge without order (Entropy), the glass without landing places (Cubes), the trail without its beginning (Walk), bins that move while values stay (Gaussian), scent vs raised terrain (Pheromone), counters vs the newest 300 marks (Examples).

The body as the test of a mark: slot plate vs withdrawn collider (Remove), ridges you walk through vs slabs you cannot (10 PRINT), the floor that removes support under you (Remove, returning in Game), the stone that leaves while you stand on it (Game).

Returning objects: the removal floor comes back "smaller now" in Random_Game; the entropy gauge stands again in Random_Space; the Trace drawing dot returns with a random offset; the 10 PRINT diagonals recur on the textile bolts (Definition) and the Molnar grids.
Every chapter opens by naming the previous room's move and closes by naming the next room's question, so the sequence reads as one walk rather than fourteen labels.

hall_notes.note: REPLAY, +1 DRAW and the seed slider separate a seed from the procedure that spends it; the textile bolts, the 1955 page and the crank are three ways to keep or lose a draw. The strongest opening in the sequence: predict-then-press throughout, every claim backed by the two loops it quotes.

The gauge, SORT and CONTRAST show what a categorical entropy keeps and forgets; then the jar, the displaced-point field, the ruin and the museum's own weathering wall make the omission bodily. The longest chapter: the DISCLOSE paragraph reads as a control manual, and the ruin section could lose a hundred words without losing a move.

The board makes filter, draw and delete three visible steps with a code excerpt for each, then the floor gives the same draw a consequence by withdrawing collision. Tight and exact; the ROW/COLUMN comparison under one seed is the sequence's best small experiment.

One BASIC line taken apart at its constant and its semicolon, then the same stream as Molnar grids, a floor of ridges, slabs at shoulder width and an ant's map. Reads well, but "Look down" arrives without a walk, and the slab wall it climaxes on is not yet in the museum's deal.

A thrown die read from orientation, a coin with gauges for its conditions, a heap that loses pieces and a field of bounded profiles: four records that forget different things. Short and clear; two desktop asides break the headset voice.

Rust that records your movement, then two stacks whose only change is accumulated turning under the hall's #study:rotation, then a tilt field that is a rule about place. Good comparison discipline; one sentence ("Nothing there turns") contradicts the field's clocked motion.

Steps proposed from the position reached, reflected at the glass, recorded in a trail the generator never reads; then a wandering drawing dot and a floor that rises where it is visited. Its best passage is the read-aloud of three lines; the self-avoiding sculpture, the paper rack and the leash go unplaced.

PAUSE, BATCH, the two laws' code, the u1 guard, the clip and BINS separate sampling, clipping and binning of the same stored values; the splatter's refused centre closes it. Precise and well paced; the clipped-count vs edge-bin distinction is a fine touch.

SHOW, SIZE, KIND and the named seed read a population's construction; then silhouettes (DRESS vs FORMS) and three couture bodies separate a wardrobe from a change of recipe. Long but earns it; one desktop aside.

White vs Perlin columns under SEED, FREQUENCY and OCTAVES, with the discipline of withholding the landscape reading. Reads as a bench note rather than a walk: no arrival, no placement, and in the built museum the bench stands in a wall row beside a plank over the hall's void.

Pollock homage, dartboard estimate, pipe and particle study each give chance a different job. Clear and honest about its limits (500 darts, 300 marks, 180 segments); opens with a curator's "returned".

Walkers whose deposits enter the next decision; ATTRACT vs AVOID at the same step count; the clipboard's optimal-route claim corrected in prose. A good argument whose two numbers (40 %, four walkers) do not match the field (30 %, five).
OCT, LAC and PER on a sine-based mixer, the independent-corner floor underfoot, the palette named as an interpretation. Short and sound; the Worley display and the returning gauge get no sentence.

Cycling stones with drawn waits and a tablet that shows the stored deadline, the removal floor returning, three doors decided before the press, a projectile field and a podium whose delays are drawn as a ridge. The sequence's strongest closing hall; one desktop aside, two unserved anchors, and a closer that skips the biome ladder.

stumbles: Random_Space_Geometry: the chapter opens "Look closely at neighbouring columns in the two small grids" with no arrival and no placement; in the map the bench sits at interactables (6,23) on a structure row that is wall, and the five works beyond it have no structure row at all, so the built hall puts them over a void beside a one-cell plank.

Randomness_10_PRINT_Algorithm: "Now return to the taller slabs near the entrance" sends the reader into a wall form that exists only in today's uncommitted map edit; both museum plans still deal the old hall (a science_screen and one floor-form structure).

Randomness_10_PRINT_Algorithm: "Look down. The newest seven rows of the screen are also under your feet" — the floor form stands at (11,12), eight cells from the printer at (3,11) where the reader was just told to stand.
Random_Cubes: "On a desktop the object is dropped rather than thrown" and "On a desktop, these are drops" — a headset reader is told about a rig they are not holding, twice.
Random_Pheromone: the quoted label "signal-guided: 40%" and "the four walkers" contradict the field, which prints 30 % and runs five walkers; a reader who checks the label loses trust in the rest.
Random_Rotate_Random_XYZ: "a low field of cubes begins to tilt" followed by "Nothing there turns" — the field pitches on a sine clock and the reader watching it is told nothing moves.
Randomness_Examples_of_Randomness: "Four works have returned to the gallery" — returned from where? A curation note in the reader's voice.

Random_Walk: "the grip from Trace" — the earlier room is Point_Trace, whose chapter has no title and never calls itself Trace; and the self-avoiding sculpture is introduced "between this cabinet and the basin" when it stands six cells off to the side with no anchor.
Random_Entropy: the DISCLOSE paragraph ("Press DISCLOSE… press it again… Keep pressing…") reads as a control manual inside an otherwise well-paced chapter.

Random_Game: "Press CUE again and all three stones carry a ring" implies only the middle stone had one before; the crossing builds the crown on all three stones from the start (random_cycle_cube.gd:709–714), so the reader looks for a difference that is not there.

keep.quote: Filter, draw, delete: three decisions that are easy to fold into one word, random, and only the middle one is.
Nothing in a draw says that it is red. Red is the use made of its place in these three calls.
A high reading is not a certificate of meaninglessness and a low one is not a certificate of value
Each cell was decided alone. Whether you can cross depends on their arrangement together. A body meets a consequence that no single draw contains.
No side of the cube bears that number. It belongs to a distribution, while the observed mean belongs to the throws made so far.
Read the order aloud. Keep where we were. Shorten the record. Put the bead where we are now.
A finite run need not contain such a draw; the model's tail is a probability, not an appointment.
Before describing a missed step as poor timing, ask where its warning was readable.

reading.handover_in: Clean. WaveFunctions_Synthesis_Lab ends on what must be retained to bring an unfamiliar result back, and Random_Definition opens by naming the five amounts and the familiar curve before turning to a patch of colour nobody would have chosen; the question (what does a name leave out of a making?) is exactly what the seed console answers. One blemish: the Synthesis Lab closer writes the next room as "Random_Definition", with an underscore, a file token rather than a room name, while every closer inside randomness writes room names as words ("In Random Gaussian", "in Random Space Geometry", "In Noise Types").
reading.handover_out: Random_Game closes "In Noise Types we will carry that question between neighbouring places", and Random_Noise_Types opens "The stones behind us could disappear. Their order of movement stayed intact; the drawn waits changed how long we had to cross" — an accurate recall of the crossing, and the plane-clipping point that follows is a fair next step from "which decisions are already made". But the museum deals Biome_Ladder_Randomness between the two (em_plan plans[76] → [77] nine biome vitrines → [78]), and neither chapter mentions it, whereas the Mushrooms closer names its cage interlude; the visitor walks a hall the book does not acknowledge before the promised next room.
